summary: Free, self-hosted resume builder that uses AI to tailor your resume and cover letter to each job description, with ATS checks and PDF export.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Resume Matcher is an open-source app that tailors your resume to each job. You upload a master resume (PDF or DOCX), paste a job description, review the AI's suggested changes, generate a cover letter and interview prep, then export a PDF from a template. It includes ATS scoring, keyword highlighting and a queue for tailoring several applications.
sixtySeconds.problem: Rewriting a resume for every application is slow. Resume Matcher drafts tailored versions from your master resume so you only review and adjust.
whoFor: Job seekers applying to many roles
People who want their data kept on their own machine
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free, self-hosted tool that works with many AI providers, including local Ollama, a Claude or ChatGPT subscription, or your coding agent with no API key.
requirements: Docker, or Python 3.14+, Node.js 26.13.1 and uv for a source install
An AI provider (Ollama, an API key, or a supported subscription)

overview: The quickest route is the official Docker image, which serves the app at localhost:3000 with the API under /api. Mount a volume to keep your data.
From source, run the Python backend with uv in one terminal and the Next.js frontend with npm in another, then configure your AI provider in Settings. Windows 11 steps are in SETUP.md.
Supported providers include Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek and Groq. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Source install needs very recent Python and Node
Always review AI edits for accuracy

install.verificationNote: Commands come from Resume Matcher's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.
prerequisites: Docker, or Python 3.14+, Node.js and uv

steps.title: Open the app
steps.body: Go to http://localhost:3000 and configure your AI provider in Settings.

steps.title: Start the backend (terminal 1)
steps.body: Edit .env to configure your AI provider.
steps.code:
cd apps/backend
cp .env.example .env
uv sync
uv run app

steps.title: Start the frontend (terminal 2)
steps.code:
cd apps/frontend
npm install
npm run dev

firstRun.title: Set your AI provider
firstRun.body: Open Settings and pick Ollama or a cloud provider.
